Facts: Defendant set fire intentionally? He was under drug-induced hallucination, used lighter to set bedding on fire. Result: property damage valued 4040 yuan. He was caught.

Question: Is this "放火" (arson) or "失火" (accidental fire)? The correction lessons: "失火" vs "放火". The key is whether there is intent to set fire (deliberate) vs accidental. In this case, he intentionally used lighter to set bedding on fire, albeit due to hallucination from drug use. He intentionally set fire, so it's arson (放火). However, need to consider mental state: under influence of drugs causing hallucination, but still intentional act? He used lighter to set fire. That is intentional act, though maybe not with malicious intent to cause damage, but still purposeful act of setting fire. In Chinese criminal law, arson requires intentional setting of fire that endangers public safety. If the fire is set in a private dwelling, still arson if intentional. The correction lesson about "失火" says: key is lack of intent to set fire; accidental due to negligence. Here there is intent (though hallucination). So label should be "放火".
